name: BlueSnap
tagline: Global payment orchestration with local acquiring in 50 countries, published regional fee schedules and intelligent routing with failover.
shortDescription: Waltham-based orchestration platform, now part of Payroc, that routes payments through local acquiring in 50 countries with 100+ payment types and currencies. US-issued cards cost 2.9% + 30 cents on the published schedule, with cross-border cards at 4.40% + 30 cents.
longDescription:
BlueSnap started life in 2001 as Plimus, rebranded in 2011, and was acquired by Payroc in October 2025, operating since as BlueSnap powered by Payroc. From Waltham, Massachusetts it runs a global payment orchestration platform: one integration reaching local card acquiring in 50 countries, more than 100 payment types and currencies, intelligent payment routing between acquirers, and automatic failover that retries a failed authorization with a secondary bank.

Pricing and how it works

Unusually for an orchestrator, BlueSnap publishes complete regional fee schedules as documents linked from its pricing page. On the US schedule, cards issued in the US cost 2.9% + 30 cents while cards issued abroad cost 4.40% + 30 cents, the premium following the card's issuing country rather than the merchant's location. Direct debit costs 0.50% + 30 cents, and local methods are priced individually. The add-on fees add up: fraud screening from 5 cents per transaction, 3-D Secure at 5 cents, the subscription engine at 0.70% of recurring value, marketplace split payments at 0.25%, manually keyed cards at an extra 0.50%, chargebacks at 25 dollars, and a 75 dollar Platform Access Fee in any month where sales fall below 5,000 dollars, waived for the first six months. Contracts are month-to-month with no early termination fee, and payouts run daily, landing two business days after settlement. Larger merchants negotiate interchange-plus or volume rates.

Who it is for

BlueSnap suits mid-size ecommerce and B2B businesses selling into multiple regions that want one contract instead of acquirer-by-acquirer setups, plus accounts receivable automation, Level 2 and 3 data support and ERP integrations with NetSuite, SAP, Chargebee and Zuora. Very small merchants trip over the monthly minimum, high-risk businesses are not the target, and merchants should model the add-on fees carefully, since the headline 2.9% understates the realistic total cost.

faqs.question: How much does BlueSnap cost?
faqs.answer: The published US schedule prices US-issued cards at 2.9% + 30 cents and cards issued outside the US at 4.40% + 30 cents, with direct debit at 0.50% + 30 cents. Add-ons are individually priced: fraud screening from 5 cents per transaction, 3-D Secure at 5 cents, the subscription engine at 0.70% of recurring value, split payments at 0.25% and keyed entry at an extra 0.50%. Higher-volume merchants negotiate interchange-plus or volume discounts.

faqs.question: Does BlueSnap have a monthly fee?
faqs.answer: Only for small accounts. A 75 dollar Platform Access Fee applies in any month where sales fall below 5,000 dollars, and it is waived for the first six months after signing. Above that threshold there is no standard monthly fee, contracts run month-to-month and there is no early termination fee.

faqs.question: How fast does BlueSnap pay out?
faqs.answer: Payouts run daily, with funds arriving two business days after settlement. An ACH transfer costs 50 cents and a wire costs 20 dollars on the US schedule, and FX fees apply when the presentment currency differs from the settlement currency.

faqs.question: Who owns BlueSnap?
faqs.answer: Payroc, a US acquirer, signed a definitive agreement in July 2025 and completed the acquisition on October 9, 2025. BlueSnap continues to operate under its own brand as BlueSnap powered by Payroc, with the deal adding Payroc's acquiring capabilities behind BlueSnap's orchestration and accounts receivable products.
